title_line: Technical Program Manager, Hardware  |  PMP  |  CSPO
summary: Program and product leader who has run hardware programs from prototype into production and owned software used in the field by thousands of people. At Lion Energy, Eric coordinated electrical, mechanical, firmware, software, and manufacturing teams to move the PPG2500 portable power station into production and take two more products through prototype, while working through tradeoffs on weight, battery configuration, packaging, and cost. At Aptive he was product owner for software used by more than 2,000 seasonal reps, coordinating about 12 developers across shared and overseas teams. He set up Agile, Scrum, Jira, and Confluence at Lion so leaders could see progress and blockers without chasing people. He wants to bring that hardware and field experience to feature programs on deployed, solar-powered site units.
skills: Testing and certification (FCC, UL, drop test)

paragraphs: Hardware programs rarely slip because of one big failure. They slip because firmware, packaging, and the factory each make a reasonable call that nobody else saw coming. Keeping those calls visible is the job I've been doing.

At Lion Energy I ran the PPG2500 portable power station from development into production and took two more products through prototype. The work was full of tradeoffs between weight, battery configuration, component placement, and cost, and my role was getting electrical, mechanical, firmware, and our manufacturers in China and Vietnam to decide together. I set up Scrum, Jira, and Confluence so leaders could see blockers without chasing people for updates. Before that, at Aptive, I owned software used by more than 2,000 reps and coordinated about 12 developers across shared and overseas teams.

But the part of this role that stands out is the field. LVT's units are solar powered and deployed in the real world, which is exactly where my returns work at Lion lived. I cut root cause investigations from months to about a week by getting field data back to engineering fast. I'd like to show you how I'd run feature programs across your deployed and next generation models. Could we talk next week?
